transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-30 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Sanjay Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood Owner), Dana Lee (CTO, Oxford Payments), Mark Thompson (Head of ML Infra), Priya Nair (SRE)

Summary (auto): Discussed latency targets (p95), concurrency for streaming product, token/sec benchmarking approach, Dedicated capacity vs Hosted vs Private deployment tradeoffs, and security/compliance items. Agreed to run a benchmark POC with 100 concurrent streams initially and scale to 1k simulated users.

Topics: p95 targets, streaming concurrency, batching/token/sec, KV cache effects, autoscale and fallback, Private deployment KMS/SSO, observability and tracing.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'll kick off, I'm Alex from Redwood, Maya's our owner but she'll chime in on pricing and logistics. Sanjay is our SE.
[00:12] Dana: Morning team. We're excited to understand performance options, really focused on latency and cost. For context we do payments auth flows and customer messaging, so p95 matters.
[00:21] Mark: Yeah, our SLA for fraud detection path is 200ms p95 end-to-end, we can afford up to 50ms for the model call ideally but that's tough.
[00:31] Sanjay: Totally. To be clear we typically talk about two numbers: model p95 and end-to-end in-app. For model-only, are you measuring short prompts ~16-64 tokens or longer? That changes kernels and batching.
[00:44] Dana: Mostly short prompts, 30 tokens average. Also streaming for messages — need streaming tail latency to be low.
[00:52] Alex: Got it. Quick qual - how many concurrent users/requests do you expect at peak?
[00:57] Priya: For peak events maybe 1k concurrent users making streaming connections, roughly 200 req/sec steady, spikes to 600 req/sec for short windows.
[01:08] Mark: And we care about token/sec throughput because of batching / cost. We run on AWS today for other infra.
[01:15] Sanjay: Ok. For Hosted we can usually hit ~50-120ms p95 for small prompts on smaller models with streaming; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and better p95 at scale due to reserved GPUs and optimized batching, Private gives full network control but needs infra ops.
[01:30] Dana: Any real-world numbers you can share for p95 and tokens/sec?
[01:34] Sanjay: Rough numbers — with Redwood Hosted on say a Llama-like 7B variant, we've seen 80-120ms p95 for 32 token prompts with streaming enabled, throughput around 1.2k tokens/sec per GPU depending on quantization and batch config. With Dedicated optimized kernels and 8-bit quant we push higher throughput and lower jitter; p95 can drop into 50-70ms for the same prompt distribution.
[01:57] Mark: That sounds promising. How does KV cache and prefix caching affect streaming latency?
[02:02] Sanjay: Good question. KV cache reduces repeated context overhead, so for chat-heavy flows with long context it's helpful. For short independent prompts, KV cache has less impact. Prefix caching helps when many requests share initial tokens, and can drop p95 by ~10-20% in some workloads. But caching has memory tradeoffs.
[02:18] Dana: Tokens/sec is an interesting metric. We want to benchmark token/sec but also p95 per token — what's the typical benchmarking harness?
[02:26] Alex: We usually run a token/sec benchmark with a mix: 70% short prompts, 30% medium, measure p50/p95/p99 across streaming and non-streaming modes, and run concurrency sweeps (50, 100, 250, 500, 1k). For Dedicated we can provision GPU nodes and simulate 1k concurrent streams to show stable p95.
[02:44] Priya: Network egress and VPC peering matter for Private — do you support VPC peering and customer KMS?
[02:51] Sanjay: Yes, Private supports VPC peering, on‑prem bundles, and KMS/HSM integrations. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key via a KMS integration. There can be different audit log retention options.
[03:02] Mark: About streaming — do you have any guidance for connection count per GPU or per node?
[03:09] Sanjay: It's workload dependent. For small token generation with streaming, you can serve hundreds of concurrent streams per GPU with low per‑stream token/sec; when throughput per request is higher, that number falls. We recommend simulated loads to find sweet spot; Dedicated lets you size predictably.
[03:24] Dana: If we aim for 150ms model p95 at 30 tokens average with 1k concurrent streams, what are the realistic deployment options?
[03:33] Sanjay: For that target, Dedicated is the likely path. Hosted might hit targets sporadically but you're sharing capacity. With Dedicated you can reserve nodes and configure autoscale/burst so p95 SLOs are much easier. Private could also meet it but will require us to work through network egress and infra sizing.
[03:48] Alex: On pricing note, Dedicated is on monthly commit, Hosted is pay-as-you-go. We'll send pricing tiers in the follow up.
[03:54] Mark: For the POC we want to test both Hosted and Dedicated to see cost vs p95. Can you run an autonomous benchmark?
[04:02] Sanjay: Yes, we can run benchmark runs. We'll need sample prompts, expected concurrency profile, and a test window. For Hosted we can run against your account or ours; for Dedicated we can set up a short reserved env.
[04:14] Dana: We can provide prompt set and traffic pattern. Also want to capture streaming tail latency and token/sec observed.
[04:20] Priya: On security, we need SOC2, SAML SSO support, RBAC, audit logs, retention settings, and optional on‑prem.
[04:29] Alex: We'll attach our SOC2 report and SSO docs. Sanjay will share Private deployment checklist.
[04:36] Mark: What's the typical time to get Dedicated up for a POC?
[04:40] Sanjay: Usually 3-7 days to provision and warm pools depending on region and availability; longer if you need specific on‑prem or air‑gapped setups.
[04:49] Dana: For token/sec benchmarking, do you provide client harness or do we run a JMeter-like load?
[04:55] Sanjay: We provide a benchmark harness (scripted), and also a documentation describing how to run distributed clients. We can run the harness from our infra to your endpoint to validate latency. Note: remote harness adds network variance; best results are from within same region.
[05:10] Mark: Can we capture GPU utilization and trace tokens/sec per GPU?
[05:13] Sanjay: Yes, in Dedicated we expose per‑node telemetry and breakdown — token/sec, GPU util, kernel latency; in Hosted we provide aggregated dashboards and sampling traces.
[05:23] Alex: Are there any regulatory / data residency constraints we should know?
[05:26] Dana: EU customers require data residency; for now mostly US and EU. Also certain logs need to be scrubbed for PII.
[05:33] Sanjay: We can support region pinning and log redaction options on Private and Dedicated.
[05:38] Priya: A couple of practical questions — streaming chunk size and chunk interval, we want small chunks (100-200ms) to improve UX. Does Redwood support that?
[05:46] Sanjay: Yes streaming chunk sizes and flush intervals are tunable; however smaller intervals increase overhead so you need to balance token/sec and latency.
[05:54] Dana: Let's talk KPI for the POC: p95 model latency <=150ms for 30 token prompts at up to 1k concurrent streams; stable token/sec per GPU >1k; streaming tail under 200ms.
[06:07] Alex: That's a good SLO. We'll propose a POC with those criteria.
[06:11] Mark: Any gotchas for quantization? We use some 8-bit quant models in prod, do you support quantized variants?
[06:17] Sanjay: Yes, we support quantized variants; kernel selection can favor int8 execution paths, and we test quality/regression. Quant sometimes changes latency characteristics slightly but reduces memory footprint and often boosts throughput.
[06:30] Priya: On observability, we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route tracing.
[06:36] Alex: Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, token cost breakdown and tracing hooks; can export traces to your observability stack.
[06:43] Dana: Ok good. What's the rollback / fallback strategy if Dedicated nodes are crowded?
[06:48] Sanjay: Smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants or to Hosted capacity if you allow bursting. Canary rollouts supported.
[06:56] Mark: For the benchmark, can you measure p95 under cache-hit and cache-miss scenarios?
[07:01] Sanjay: Yes, we'll design runs for cold KV cache vs warm cache; that gives realistic variance.
[07:08] Dana: How will we verify streaming tail latency measurement? Are you instrumenting from client perspective?
[07:13] Sanjay: We'll measure from client perspective as well as in‑node metrics to correlate.
[07:18] Alex: Quick note, sometimes transcripts call our product names oddly — Redwood Dedicated sometimes shows up as 'Redwould' in notes, so ignore that.
[07:25] (laughter)
[07:28] Dana: Haha noted. A couple more questions: can you do BYOK with HSM?
[07:33] Sanjay: Yes, Private supports HSM/backed KMS and some enterprise customers use that for encryption at rest keys.
[07:40] Priya: For network, can we have VPC peering and private routes? We prefer not to expose endpoints over public internet for the POC.
[07:47] Sanjay: Yes for Private and Dedicated we can arrange VPC peering. Hosted can support private endpoints in some regions. We'll document options.
[07:57] Mark: Great. Let's capture next steps.
[08:00] Alex: Recap: We'll send pricing tiers and Dedicated options, Sanjay will share SOC2 + Private checklist, customer will send prompt set and traffic profile, and we schedule benchmark for early Oct.
[08:12] Dana: Confirming POC success criteria again: p95 <=150ms model latency for 30 token prompts at up to 1k concurrent streaming, token/sec per GPU >1k, streaming tail <200ms.
[08:23] Alex: Yep. We'll draft POC and include test plan.
[08:26] Mark: Anything else?
[08:28] Priya: Just one ask — please include a sample run showing GPU-util vs token/sec so we can estimate cost.
[08:34] Sanjay: Will do. We'll share an anonymized benchmark spreadsheet with kernel-level breakdown.
[08:40] Dana: Thanks — that covers most of it.
[08:43] Alex: Thanks all. We'll follow up with docs and schedule.
[08:47] (call wraps, small crosstalk)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional misheard acronyms (e.g., HSM -> 'ash-em'), product names sometimes mis-cased, filler words present.

References/Links mentioned: Redwood Dedicated pricing doc (link TBD), SOC2 report (attachment pending), POC benchmark harness (link TBD).

End of transcript.
